# Code of Conduct

This document is written in English and is the authoritative version. There is no German
translation (see [`docs/i18n.md`](../docs/i18n.md)).

## The point

This project argues about work in writing, often bluntly. Reviews here say things like "this proof
never ran on Linux" and "this gate can never be red". That directness is aimed at **the work** and is
the reason the documentation can be trusted. It is not licence to aim it at people.

The distinction is the whole code of conduct. Everything below follows from it.

## Expected

- **Criticise the artefact, not the author.** "This test would pass with the feature removed" is
  useful. "You always write useless tests" is not, and it also says less.
- **Bring the counter-proof.** If you think something is wrong, show the case where it breaks. Being
  shown to be wrong with evidence is the good outcome, not the embarrassing one.
- **Say what you do not know.** "I could not reproduce this" and "I did not run that command" are
  full contributions. Guessing confidently is not.
- **Assume competence and time pressure.** Most mistakes in this repository were made by people
  paying attention, under load, with incomplete information — including the ones written up in the
  readiness protocol.
- **Accept a decision once it is made**, or reopen it explicitly with new information. Re-litigating
  by attrition is not disagreement, it is obstruction.
- **Respect that not everyone reads German.** The design documentation is German; contribution does
  not require it. Do not make someone's language a reason to dismiss their input, in either
  direction.

## Not acceptable

- Personal attacks, insults, or demeaning comments — including ones dressed as technical feedback.
- Harassment of any kind: sexualised language or imagery, unwanted attention, stalking, or
  deliberately intimidating behaviour, in the repository or elsewhere in connection with it.
- Discrimination or derogatory remarks based on age, body, disability, ethnicity, sex
  characteristics, gender identity or expression, experience level, education, socio-economic
  status, nationality, appearance, race, religion, or sexual orientation.
- Publishing someone's private information without their explicit permission.
- Sustained disruption: derailing threads, repeated bad-faith argument, or brigading a decision.
- Retaliation against anyone who reports a problem under this document.

## Scope

Applies in every project space — issues, pull requests, discussions, commit messages, code comments,
documentation — and to anyone representing the project in public.

## Reporting

Report privately to the maintainer, **@LupusMalusDeviant**, through GitHub. If the matter also
involves a security vulnerability, use
[private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/LupusMalusDeviant/bifrost/security/advisories/new)
instead, which is a properly confidential channel.

> **Stated plainly, because it matters to anyone deciding whether to report:** this is a small,
> single-maintainer project. There is no separate conduct committee, no dedicated contact address
> published yet, and no independent appeal path. A report goes to the same person who maintains the
> code. If that is not an acceptable channel for what you need to report, GitHub's own
> [reporting mechanisms](https://docs.github.com/communities/maintaining-your-safety-on-github)
> exist and are independent of this project.

Reports will be handled as confidentially as the above allows. Reporters will not be named to the
person reported about without their agreement.

## Consequences

Depending on severity and pattern: a private correction, a public correction, a temporary block from
interaction, or a permanent ban from the project's spaces. The maintainer decides, and will say what
was decided to the reporter.

## Attribution

This document is written for this project rather than adopted from a template. It is informed by the
[Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/), which is worth reading if you want the
widely-used baseline that many projects adopt verbatim.
